events.credibility_reason: Withdrawn by the author on 18 Jun 2025 (arXiv v2); the integer case it claimed is in any case near-trivial per the author's own comment.

why: Only three events fall after 26 Jan 2024. Kumar's integer-only claim would be a case at most, but the author withdrew it, so it is knocked down. Moniri's abstract only announces future work, so it scores none. Lu-Zheng treats the negative base -3/2, which makes it a variant. The pre-snapshot events are counting bounds (Mahler, Flatto), the 1/3 oscillation bound (FLP 1995), a conditional consequence (Strauch), and results on other bases or parity sets (Tijdeman, Dubickas, Akiyama). None of them settles the question. The close call was FLP 1995 under the 1/q reading, which would make it a pre-snapshot resolution. The weight of quotations, plus every later source calling the problem open, supports 1/p, so I scored it as a bound. Dubickas 2009 extends the 1/p bound to other bases, and for 3/2 it gives the same 1/3, so I treated it as a variant and not a new bound. No AI was involved in any event.
doubts: The FLP 1995 1/p versus 1/q discrepancy is unresolved in the record. The literal statement is false at x = 0, while the literature restricts to x > 0; I judged against the positive-real reading. Moniri's full text was unread and might contain a result.
